summary: Hyejeong Choi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Ohio State University (attested 2015) under John C. Huntington. Choi held a post as a Visiting Researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara.

Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Freiburg (~1985–1986), Yale University (~1983–1987), and Harvard University (~1989–1992). He also trained under traditional teacher Seungsahn Haengwon from circa 1990 to 2004.

Hyoung Seok Ham is an Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Virginia (2010) and earned a PhD at the University of Michigan (attested 2016) under doctoral supervisor Madhav M. Deshpande.

Hywel David Lewis (1910–1992) worked in philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Bangor University (~1929–1933) and Jesus College, Oxford (~1933–1935), later serving on the faculty at Bangor University from circa 1936 to 1955.

Hürelbaatar Ujeed is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who earned a PhD in Social Anthropology from the University of Cambridge. He has served as Professor and Principal Investigator at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.
Hōin Yamada (born 1940) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University and trained under Gyōin Hashimoto.
Hōju (born 1980) works in Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University (~1999–2005) and KU Leuven (~2005–2007).

Ian Harris (1952–2014) was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar educated at Cambridge (~1970–1973) and Lancaster (~1980–1985). He held posts at St Martin's College (~1988–2007) and the University of Cumbria (attested 2000–2014) as Professor Emeritus.

Ian James Coghlan works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University by 2004 and served as a research fellow at the Monash Asia Institute at Monash University (attested 2005).
Ian Kishizawa (1865–1955) was a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Saitama University and trained under traditional teacher Sotan Oka.

Ian Mabbett (1939–2020) was a historian, Indologist, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at Oxford (~1960–1963). He served as Reader in History at Monash University (~1965–2004) and Professor of Indian and Buddhist Studies at Aichi Bunkyo University (2000).

Ian Reader (born 1949) specializes in religious studies and Japanology. After earning his doctorate at the University of Leeds (~1978–1983), he taught at Kansai Gaidai University (~1984–1989), University of Stirling (~1989–1999), and Lancaster University (~1999–2006).

Ibrahim Shah is an archaeology scholar who earned a PhD at the University of Peshawar by 2007. He serves at Hazara University as Associate Professor and Chairman of the Department of Cultural Heritage and Tourism Management.
Ichijo Ogawa (born 1936) specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He studied at Otani University (~1955–1959), where he later served as president (~1969–2004).

Ichiro Hori (1910–1974) was a religious studies, Buddhist studies, and history scholar educated at the University of Tokyo. He studied under Kunio Yanagita and held teaching posts at Tohoku University (~1953–1965) and the University of Tokyo (1965–1971).

Ichiro Katayama (born 1942) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied under Kogen Mizuno and at Komazawa and Otani universities. He served as an associate professor at Komazawa University from 1975 to 2013.

Ichisada Miyazaki (1901–1995) was a scholar of Sinology and history. He studied at Kyoto University (~1922–1925) under Jitsuzo Kuwabara (~1922–1931) and later held an academic post at Kyoto University from circa 1936 to 1965.
Ignazio Guidi (1844–1935) studied at the University of Rome from circa 1864 to 1869, later serving there as a professor from 1876 to 1919.

Igor Dmitrievich Serebryakov (1917–1998) worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Saint Petersburg State University (~1936–1941) and served at the Institute of Oriental Studies of the Russian Academy of Sciences from circa 1960 to 1998.

Ihsan Ali (born 1955) is an archaeology and Indology scholar educated at the University of Peshawar and under Raymond Allchin (~1989–1993). He served as Director of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Directorate of Archaeology and Museums (~2002–2005) and Vice Chancellor of Hazara University (~2006–2009).
